notes: Migration-pair ruleset v1 (Data-Tier Oracle Program, Spec O). Pair knowledge lives HERE as data — generic code never names an engine. Rules with a `comparison` block drive the data-parity comparator and diff classification; guidance-only rules (comparison: null) carry rewrite/seed knowledge. `construct_refs` key pair guidance to the discovery-side sqlDialectClassifier's stable construct names (the classifier is pack code and remains the detector).

rules.title: Sybase datetime carries 1/300s precision; Postgres timestamp is microseconds
rules.rewrite_guidance: Values loaded from Sybase datetime can never carry sub-1/300s precision; the target must not synthesise finer precision (e.g. via now()/clock_timestamp() defaults) on like-for-like paths.
rules.scenario_seed: Round-trip a timestamp whose milliseconds are not a multiple of 1/300s and assert the persisted+returned value matches the source system's rounding.

rules.title: Sybase smalldatetime has minute precision
rules.rewrite_guidance: smalldatetime maps to timestamp(0) at best; compare at minute granularity.
rules.scenario_seed: Write a value with seconds set and verify the returned value truncates to the minute exactly as the source does.

rules.title: Sybase char/varchar comparison ignores trailing spaces; empty string inserts as a single space
rules.rewrite_guidance: Sybase stores '' as ' ' in (var)char and treats trailing spaces as insignificant in equality. Postgres preserves both. Loads and WHERE-clause rewrites must not let '' vs ' ' or padded values become spurious mismatches — right-trimmed equality is the like-for-like contract.
rules.scenario_seed: Persist an empty string and a trailing-space value through the API; assert lookup/equality behaviour matches the source system on both.

rules.title: Sybase money/smallmoney is fixed 4-decimal scale
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map to numeric(19,4)/numeric(10,4); never to floating types. Rounding at scale 4 is part of the observed contract.
rules.scenario_seed: Write an amount requiring rounding at the 4th decimal and assert identical rounding behaviour.

rules.title: float/real representational differences across engines
rules.rewrite_guidance: Bit-identical float round-trips are not guaranteed across engines; equality within relative epsilon is the honest contract. Columns needing exactness must migrate to numeric.
rules.scenario_seed: Round-trip values with no exact binary representation (e.g. 0.1 accumulations) and compare within tolerance.

rules.title: Legacy Sybase charsets (cp850/iso_1/roman8) convert to UTF-8 on load
rules.rewrite_guidance: Compare after Unicode NFC normalisation; conversion may change byte length (column overflow risk on load) without changing the logical value.
rules.scenario_seed: Round-trip accented/extended characters present in the estate's data and assert logical equality plus no truncation.

rules.title: Case-insensitive Sybase sort orders vs Postgres case-sensitive default collations
rules.rewrite_guidance: Only applies to estates configured with a case-insensitive sort order. Equality, uniqueness and ORDER BY semantics all shift; target needs citext/ICU collation or expression indexes to preserve behaviour.
rules.scenario_seed: Lookup by a key differing only in case; assert hit/miss parity with the source system.

rules.title: Sybase bit is non-nullable; Postgres boolean is nullable
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map bit -> boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false to preserve the source's it-can-never-be-null contract; a nullable boolean silently widens the state space.
rules.scenario_seed: Attempt writes that omit the flag and assert the default/constraint behaviour matches the source.

rules.title: Sybase tinyint is unsigned 0..255; Postgres has no unsigned single-byte type
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map to smallint + CHECK (0..255) to preserve the range contract; values 128..255 are legal in the source data.
rules.scenario_seed: Write boundary values 0, 255 and an out-of-range attempt; assert identical accept/reject behaviour.

rules.title: text/image map to text/bytea with different length and NULL semantics
rules.rewrite_guidance: image -> bytea compares byte-exact (no normalisation); text/unitext compare after charset conversion. Sybase readtext/writetext idioms have no direct equivalent.
rules.scenario_seed: Round-trip a large text payload and a binary payload; assert byte/logical equality respectively.
rules.notes: image moved to SYBPG.BIN.001 (2026-08-07): binary data must compare byte-exact, never charset-normalised.

rules.title: Identity gaps and @@identity scope differ across engines
rules.rewrite_guidance: Generated ids are volatility, not oracle: mark identity columns as excluded-by-volatility in comparisons. Sequences must be resynced above MAX(id) after load; identity burn/gap behaviour differs and must not be asserted.
rules.scenario_seed: Fail an insert mid-transaction then insert successfully; assert the OBSERVABLE contract (uniqueness, monotonicity if relied upon) rather than specific values.

rules.title: numeric/decimal exact-value canonical form
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map to numeric(19,4)/numeric(10,4); never to floating types. Rounding at scale 4 is part of the observed contract.
rules.scenario_seed: Write an amount requiring rounding at the 4th decimal and assert identical rounding behaviour.
rules.notes: 2026-08-07 (gold standard C5): both wires carry numeric/decimal as strings; trailing-zero scale differences ('123.40' vs '123.4') are canonicalised WITHOUT float parsing so precision is preserved and only real value drift diverges.

rules.title: binary byte-exact hex comparison
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map to numeric(19,4)/numeric(10,4); never to floating types. Rounding at scale 4 is part of the observed contract.
rules.scenario_seed: Write an amount requiring rounding at the 4th decimal and assert identical rounding behaviour.
rules.notes: 2026-08-07 (gold standard C5): Sybase wire renders binary as '\x'+lowercase hex; node-pg renders bytea as a Buffer - both canonicalise to the same hex string, so equality is byte-exact.

rules.title: ASE date/time/bigdatetime/bigtime epoch canonical form
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map to numeric(19,4)/numeric(10,4); never to floating types. Rounding at scale 4 is part of the observed contract.
rules.scenario_seed: Write an amount requiring rounding at the 4th decimal and assert identical rounding behaviour.
rules.notes: 2026-08-07 (gold standard C5): the ASE date/time family previously had NO rule - textual shape differences ('13:05:09' vs '13:05:09.000', '2026-01-31' vs '2026-01-31 00:00:00') diverged falsely. Second-granularity epoch canonical form.

rules.title: Shape-adaptive calling convention for translated procedures and functions

convention.function_name: routine name, lower case, in the mapped target schema
convention.arg_naming: source parameter name without the @ sigil, lower case, source order
convention.out_param_naming: same as arg_naming; OUTPUT parameters become OUT arguments

shapes.return_status: no result set, no OUTPUT parameter: RETURNS integer (the RETURN value; 0 when the source returns nothing)
shapes.single_result_set: exactly one result-producing SELECT and a trivial return status: RETURNS TABLE(<columns of that SELECT>) / SETOF; the existing {call}+executeQuery JDBC pattern keeps working
shapes.out_params: OUTPUT parameters and no result set: OUT arguments (plus OUT return_status when the status is non-trivial); the registered-parameter JDBC pattern keeps working
shapes.rich: more than one result set, or a result set combined with OUTPUT parameters or a non-trivial return status: OUT refcursor arguments rs1..rsN in source order + OUT return_status + OUT parameters; the caller must run inside a transaction and FETCH ALL from each cursor

convention.selection: rich when max_result_sets > 1 or (max_result_sets == 1 and (has_output_params or not return_status_trivial)); single_result_set when max_result_sets == 1; out_params when has_output_params; otherwise return_status

rules.rewrite_guidance: Emit EXACTLY the header the descriptor prescribes (name, argument names/order/types, OUT arguments, RETURNS clause). Keep every ORDER BY. Lower-case unquoted identifiers. Never add behaviour the source lacks.
rules.scenario_seed: Invoke through the descriptor's shape on the target and compare the full envelope (return status, OUT values, every result set, messages, state delta) against the captured baseline.
rules.notes: 2026-09-09 (Stored Proc & Function Behaviour Program, Spec 2): the first three shapes keep the application's existing pgjdbc call patterns working (DB-only migrations); only `rich` forces a Java-side change and no Postgres shape avoids it.

rules.title: RAISERROR carries its source error number and severity through a fixed SQLSTATE

convention.raise_form: RAISE EXCEPTION USING ERRCODE = 'P0001', MESSAGE = <text>, DETAIL = '{"source_error": <n>, "severity": <s>, "state": <st>}'

rules.rewrite_guidance: Every RAISERROR becomes RAISE EXCEPTION with SQLSTATE P0001 and a DETAIL JSON carrying the source number/severity/state; the message text is carried verbatim. Never map business errors onto engine SQLSTATEs.
rules.scenario_seed: Drive each RAISERROR site and assert the same source error number surfaces on both engines.
rules.notes: 2026-09-09 (Spec 2). The comparator matches on DETAIL.source_error; message text is advisory (SYBPG.PROC.MSG.001). Java code branching on Sybase error numbers is a flagged call site (SYBPG.PROC.CALLSITE.001).

rules.title: PRINT and informational messages become RAISE NOTICE and are advisory in comparison
rules.rewrite_guidance: PRINT <text> becomes RAISE NOTICE '%', <text>. Message text differences never fail a comparison on their own.
rules.scenario_seed: Drive a PRINT path and confirm the notice is captured on both sides.

rules.title: Result-set rows compare ordered only when the producing SELECT carries ORDER BY
rules.rewrite_guidance: Keep every ORDER BY exactly; never add one the source lacks (row order without ORDER BY is engine-dependent and is compared as a multiset).
rules.scenario_seed: Drive a result set whose SELECT has no ORDER BY and confirm the multiset comparison; drive one with ORDER BY on a tie and confirm the tiebreak.

rules.title: Result-set column names compare case-insensitively; translations emit lower-case unquoted names
rules.rewrite_guidance: Emit lower-case, unquoted column aliases matching the source select list; pgjdbc column lookup is case-insensitive so DB-only call sites keep working.
rules.scenario_seed: Confirm every source column name is present (case-insensitively) and in the same position.

rules.title: Result-set and OUT-parameter cells compare under the column-type rules via a driver-type map
rules.rewrite_guidance: Not a rewrite rule: the comparator maps each engine's reported cell type onto the ruleset column-type vocabulary so DT/STR/NUM/BIT/BIN rules apply to envelope cells exactly as to table cells.
rules.scenario_seed: n/a

rules.title: Transaction control inside a routine maps to sub-blocks; an inner ROLLBACK raises

convention.inner_begin_commit: BEGIN ... EXCEPTION ... END sub-block (savepoint semantics); no COMMIT inside a function
convention.inner_rollback: RAISE EXCEPTION USING ERRCODE = 'P0002', MESSAGE = 'source routine rolled back' — the caller's transaction aborts, as the source's outer transaction did

rules.rewrite_guidance: PL/pgSQL functions cannot commit; translate BEGIN TRAN/COMMIT to sub-blocks and ROLLBACK to a P0002 raise. Never emit COMMIT/ROLLBACK inside the function body.
rules.scenario_seed: Drive the inner-rollback path and assert the caller observes an aborted transaction on both engines.

rules.title: Clock-derived cells are volatility: compared as non-null timestamps within the run window
rules.rewrite_guidance: getdate() becomes now()/clock_timestamp() per SYBPG.DT.001 precision; the comparator never asserts equality of clock values captured at different wall times.
rules.scenario_seed: Capture a clock-bearing result twice and confirm the volatility evidence marks the cell.
rules.notes: 2026-09-09 (Spec 2). Applies only to cells the profile or the double-fire evidence flags as clock-derived — never a blanket mask.

rules.title: Random / generated-id cells are volatility: compared by presence only
rules.rewrite_guidance: newid() becomes gen_random_uuid(); rand() becomes random(). Values are never asserted equal.
rules.scenario_seed: Confirm the cell is non-null on both sides.
rules.notes: 2026-09-09 (Spec 2). Identity values remain governed by SYBPG.SEQ.001.

rules.title: Capture connections apply the application driver's session defaults explicitly
rules.rewrite_guidance: Behaviour that depends on a session option (ANSI null comparison, arithmetic abort, string truncation) must be reproduced explicitly on the target; the translator treats these SET values as the source semantics.
rules.scenario_seed: n/a — the profile is applied on every capture connection and recorded in the envelope.
rules.notes: 2026-09-09 (Spec 2). The list equals ASE login defaults as jConnect leaves them; the sidecar defaults to jTDS, so the SETs are applied explicitly regardless of driver. PROC_CALL_SESSION_SET overrides the list (semicolon-separated).

rules.title: JDBC call-pattern compatibility per target shape

return_status.exec_text: needs_change: EXEC text is T-SQL; call SELECT <function>() instead
return_status.error_number_branching: needs_change: Sybase error numbers arrive in SQLSTATE P0001 DETAIL, not getErrorCode()

single_result_set.jdbc_call_return: needs_change: a set-returning function has no return value; drop the ? = and read the result set
single_result_set.exec_text: needs_change: EXEC text is T-SQL; SELECT * FROM <function>(...) instead
single_result_set.error_number_branching: needs_change: Sybase error numbers arrive in SQLSTATE P0001 DETAIL, not getErrorCode()

out_params.jdbc_call_return: needs_change: the return status is an OUT argument named return_status, not the ? = slot
out_params.exec_text: needs_change: EXEC text is T-SQL; SELECT * FROM <function>(...) instead
out_params.error_number_branching: needs_change: Sybase error numbers arrive in SQLSTATE P0001 DETAIL, not getErrorCode()

rich.jdbc_call_return: needs_change: refcursor shape — run inside a transaction and register OUT cursor parameters (Types.REF_CURSOR)
rich.jdbc_call: needs_change: refcursor shape — run inside a transaction and register OUT cursor parameters (Types.REF_CURSOR)
rich.exec_text: needs_change: refcursor shape — run inside a transaction and register OUT cursor parameters (Types.REF_CURSOR)
rich.bare_reference: needs_change: refcursor shape — run inside a transaction and register OUT cursor parameters (Types.REF_CURSOR)
rich.error_number_branching: needs_change: Sybase error numbers arrive in SQLSTATE P0001 DETAIL, not getErrorCode()

rules.rewrite_guidance: Service-plane rewrites read the per-routine descriptor and this matrix; call sites classified compatible keep their code, needs_change sites carry the named change.
rules.scenario_seed: n/a — deterministic classification of code-scan call sites.
rules.notes: 2026-09-09 (Spec 2). Patterns are classified from the code scan's proc-call query text: `{? = call` → jdbc_call_return, `{call` → jdbc_call, `exec`/`execute` text → exec_text, a bare routine reference (SimpleJdbcCall / prepareCall by name) → bare_reference (honest unknown).

construct_refs.seed: Freeze/inject clock or mark timestamp fields volatile; getdate() precision follows SYBPG.DT.001.
Probe NULL-argument paths: isnull(x,y) typing follows the FIRST arg in T-SQL, coalesce follows the highest type — seed a scenario where the types differ.
Seed each convert() style code in use — date style codes (103, 112 etc.) have no direct to_char equivalent and formatting is response-visible.
Seed an insert-through-trigger path: @@identity in T-SQL sees the LAST identity including triggers; the rewrite must preserve which id the app observed.
Seed an update-zero-rows path; branch logic on @@rowcount must behave identically.
Seed a constraint-violation path; vendor error-code branching must map to the equivalent condition, and the API-visible error body is part of the oracle.
Seed a TOP-n query on a tie: without a deterministic ORDER BY tiebreak the selected rows may legitimately differ — the rewrite must add the tiebreak the app implicitly relied on.
Concurrency detour: lock-hint semantics do not map onto MVCC; seed a two-session scenario if the estate relies on blocking reads.
NOLOCK dirty reads have no MVCC equivalent; the like-for-like target reads committed data — seed only to document the intentional divergence.
Seed the proc paths using #temp tables end-to-end; scoping and implicit creation semantics differ.
Seed the error path: raiserror severity/message formatting is response-visible where procs surface errors to the API.
SET ROWCOUNT limits DML in T-SQL; seed the affected update path — silent partial updates are a data-integrity trap.
*= joins can silently become inner joins in naive rewrites; seed rows that only appear via the outer side.
